sources.quote: Source is in English; no translation needed. Note on the rule field: patterns are determinate only for the source's clean window, lengths 2-4 (Table 2.9, p. 72). Primary stress is fixed initial and weight-blind at all lengths, but for lengths 5-8 secondary-stress placement is not one pattern per length (varies within each length; possible weight/vowel-quality conditioning left uninvestigated by the author), so those lengths are off the map. sources.quote: Primary stress on the initial syllable of the phonological word; correlates intensity and sometimes pitch, not duration; epenthetic schwa can bear stress; 2/3/4-syllable words = trochee/dactyl/ditrochee (ˈσσ, ˈσσσ, ˈσσˌσσ); secondary stress in 5+σ (all polymorphemic) words varies and 'remains to be investigated'; stated exceptions: partial reduplication (rrokar [rə̆ˈrokar]) and verbal proclitics (outside the phonological word, p. 127).
